item_title: Product-design challenge lab (AltMeat: Product Design of Plant-Based Foods), with a technical foundations course and the Collider Cup showcase
owner: Alt: Meat Lab and SCET, UC Berkeley
scope_note: Teaching and venture building for protein for people
vietnam_angle: Yes. Product-development skills tied to buyer problems is a gap that no study public good covers (P1, P4, P5, P6 are rules, a laboratory and data; RM-09 is process engineering). T1 and T10 need buyer specifications and functional trials before a plant. A national platform for student food innovation already exists.
vietnam_evidence: HUIT's Food Innovation and Development (FID) contest 2025: nearly 500 contestants, 144 projects from 58 universities and high schools, a firm-judged table with 10 enterprise prizes, co-organised by VAFoST and the National Startup Support Center; no plant-protein product among the 2025 winners (AML-33). A 2023 season had a plant-based theme (snippet only, AML-34). ch06 records almost no Vietnamese work on sensory and structure of meat analogues. We found no credit-bearing Vietnamese course with alternative-protein content (one search; L6 owns the inventory).
verdict_note: Proposed as AML-C1 (buyer-set protein product challenge lab), balanced score 2.95 (our calculation). Berkeley ran the format from Spring 2017 to Spring 2024: 4-unit classes, entry by application, simulated startup teams on industry-set problems, about 32 students a semester, at least three startups. Merge with any L6 proposal under GFI-023 or GFI-024.
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese chay maker, plant-milk maker or fermenter sets and pays for a student problem at FID or at a food-technology faculty; L6 course inventory
source_ids: AML-04; AML-07; AML-18; AML-21; AML-22; AML-33; AML-34; BUY-44

item_title: Customer needfinding challenge lab (Product Design and Customer Needfinding: Alternative Meat)
owner: Alt: Meat Lab and SCET, UC Berkeley
scope_note: Consumer needfinding as a design input is in scope (Part III); consumer marketing plans are not
vietnam_angle: Weak. Vietnam needs sensory and choice-test capacity, which DMV-03 already proposes at HUST, NIN and Can Tho University.
vietnam_evidence: Four sections, Fall 2019 to Fall 2023, 135 students enrolled in total (AML-22). No Vietnamese counterpart searched beyond FID.
verdict_note: Covered by DMV-03. Could be a module of AML-C1 rather than a separate course.
signal_to_watch: Vietnamese universities publish blind tests of higher-protein chay or blends (DMV-03)

item_title: Free public webinar course: Plant-Based Foods: critical analysis of production methods, sustainability, nutrition and health
scope_note: Consumer education is outside the supply-side scope; the technical content is in scope
vietnam_angle: None specific. Aimed at United States consumers; the study's own pages and briefs inform Vietnamese readers.
vietnam_evidence: Three 2-hour online sessions on how meat, milk, butter and cheese analogues are made (AML-16). No recording or slides found on the lab site.
verdict_note: No Vietnamese use that the study's pages do not already serve.

item_title: Plant-based seafood collider: 8-week R&D roadmap challenge, species to include carp, tilapia, salmon or catfish
owner: Alt: Meat Lab and SCET, with SeaCo and GFI
vietnam_angle: Weak. Catfish and tilapia are Vietnamese farmed species, but Vietnam exports pangasius and has no named buyer for a plant-based catfish analogue; alternative seafood sits with L4.
vietnam_evidence: Eight teams (AML-09); the winners founded Terramino Foods, now Prime Roots (AML-10; AML-11). No Vietnamese evidence sought here.
verdict_note: No Vietnam-specific buyer or asset for a plant-based catfish analogue. See L4 on surimi and species choice.
signal_to_watch: L4 finds a buyer for plant or hybrid seafood made in Vietnam

item_title: Industry-sponsored localisation and ingredient projects: plant-based egg powder rebuilt from Brazilian plants for Mantiqueira (2020); corn and oat protein ingredient design and a plant-based hard-boiled egg (2022)
vietnam_angle: Yes, as a method. Vinamilk's high-protein plant line uses imported pea protein, and T10 needs a buyer specification and a functional match. A buyer-sponsored student project is a cheap way to test rice or mung bean protein against that specification.
vietnam_evidence: Mantiqueira asked that its updated plant egg be made with Brazilian plants (AML-05). Vietnamese buyer: Vinamilk uses imported pea protein (FORM-01). TPP-05's current first test is functional samples to two dairy research teams.
verdict_note: Adds to T10 and TPP-05 a first-test format: a buyer sets a specification and a university team characterises local protein against it. No result of the Berkeley projects was published.
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese plant-milk maker commissions a university project on rice or mung bean protein

item_title: Givaudan technical challenge: a plant-based product with intracellular fat and water
scope_note: Fat and moisture systems for plant protein foods
vietnam_angle: Weak. Juiciness matters for chay analogues, but this is generic formulation science and L1 owns fat systems.
verdict_note: Vietnam would buy the method. No open result exists to transfer.
signal_to_watch: An open method for fat and water retention in dry textured soy products

item_title: Berkeley Food Institute partnership: comparison of bean varieties on growing, processing, nutrition and taste
owner: Alt: Meat Lab and Berkeley Food Institute
vietnam_angle: Weak. The study already chose mung bean and rice for T10 and set P4 for protein-quality data.
verdict_note: Covered by T10 and P4. The method is a simple multi-criteria crop comparison.

item_title: Student project to remove the beany and bitter aftertaste of pea protein by gene editing
vietnam_angle: None specific. Vietnam does not grow pea; it would buy improved pea protein, not make it.
verdict_note: Gene-edited crops abroad; Vietnam is a taker.
signal_to_watch: Commercial low-off-flavour pea protein that lowers the price T10 must beat

item_title: Partnership with Thimus on food neuroscience and cultural aspects of food
owner: Alt: Meat Lab with Thimus (Italy and United States)
scope_note: Consumer neuroscience is closer to marketing than supply; cultural fit is a design input
vietnam_angle: None specific. Proprietary tools; no published method.
verdict_note: No transferable method. Sensory capacity is covered by DMV-03.

item_title: Podcast note on shear (Couette) cell texturisation, with a Wageningen University researcher
vietnam_angle: None beyond what L1 screens under GFI-025. T1 starts with dry extrusion; high-moisture and fibrous texture come later.
vietnam_evidence: Podcast note only; audio not reviewed.
verdict_note: Covered by T1 (high-moisture extrusion later) and the L1 screen of GFI-025.

item_title: Alumni startup Prime Roots (formerly Terramino Foods): koji mycelium deli meats
vietnam_angle: Yes, as a signal for T9. Koji mycelium foods have reached commercial deli and foodservice sale, and a Philippine food group invested. Vietnam has a tuong tradition and local gene tools for Aspergillus oryzae.
vietnam_evidence: Seed USD 4.25 million in 2018 (AML-11); Series B USD 30 million in May 2023, USD 50 million in total, with Monde Nissin among investors (AML-29). Monde Nissin later wrote down and downsized its own meat-alternatives business (RDL-40; AIS-44).
verdict_note: Adds a global commercial precedent to T9's 'why'. It does not change T9's kill tests: strain safety data and sensory acceptance stay decisive.
signal_to_watch: An Asian food group licenses or builds koji mycelium food capacity in Southeast Asia

item_title: Alumni startup Impact Food: plant-based raw tuna
vietnam_angle: None specific. A premium analogue for United States sushi outlets; the study does not recommend premium imported-style analogues as a first business (section 26.6).
vietnam_evidence: Hult Prize 2020 (AML-14); on the menu of a three-outlet restaurant chain from March 2023 (AML-13). Later status not found.
verdict_note: Premium analogue route; see section 26.6 and L4.

item_title: Alumni startup Uncracked: plant-based crab, then seaweed-derived clean-label ingredients (emulsifier, protein binder, fortifier)
scope_note: Seaweed ingredients for plant protein foods
vietnam_angle: Possible, later. Seaweed protein for food is gap 8 in section 6.3, and Vietnam farms seaweed, but Uncracked publishes no species or composition data.
vietnam_evidence: Collider Cup XII winner in 2023 (AML-15); pivot to seaweed ingredients by June 2024 (AML-30).
signal_to_watch: Uncracked or a peer publishes seaweed functional data or licenses its platform; trials on Vietnamese seaweed

verdict_note: The only alternative-protein output by lab-affiliated authors we found. Nothing in it changes a Vietnamese decision.

item_title: Lab director and staff papers on Quillaja saponaria saponins: salmon disease, vaccine adjuvant QS-21, leaf polyphenols
owner: Lab director, postdoctoral scholar and co-authors

item_title: Berkeley Master of Bioprocess Engineering: two-semester professional master's with a pilot-scale capstone (300 L bioreactor) and industry co-teaching; lists the Alt: Meat product-design course as an elective
item_type: degree programme linked to the lab
owner: College of Chemistry, UC Berkeley (on the lab's advisory committee)
vietnam_angle: Yes. Senior process talent is the named bottleneck and T5 has a utilisation kill test. A pilot line that also serves a teaching capstone gets a steady anchor user.
vietnam_evidence: We found no open, food-grade pilot fermenter in Vietnam (INF-02; INF-05). MOST names senior process talent as the bottleneck (ECF-39). Decision 1002/QD-TTg sets high-tech workforce targets (ECF-41). One Uncracked founder came from this master's (AML-15).
verdict_note: Adds to RM-09 a concrete design (upstream, downstream, GMP and quality courses plus a pilot capstone, industry co-teaching) and to T5 a first user: teaching. Not costed.
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese university and a T5 host agree a pilot-line teaching capstone
